title: Multi-Motif Discovery Ecology, Independent Generator Competition, Moderator Separation, Negative-World Search & Cross-Motif Law-Composition Court

forbidden: choosing worlds because they fit one motif

A.prior_status: P7 absorbed generic family; P8 may use it only as one competitor, not as new novelty

B.raw_shape: some state changes are invalid unless a required companion fact/artifact becomes durable with them; other adjacent follow-up actions are intentionally outside the closure boundary

C.raw_shape: shared authority or credentials can widen failure/security blast radius; some resources are scoped to an instance/fleet while genuinely shared resources remain shared

negative_world_requirements.A: find a case where duplicated/parallel representations are intentionally distinct or mechanically derived so convergence would be wrong
negative_world_requirements.B: find a case where adjacent operations are intentionally outside one atomic closure because they do not share the invariant or atomic substrate is unavailable
negative_world_requirements.C: find a case where sharing authority/resources is intentionally retained because the semantics or operational domain is genuinely shared

competition_questions: When does convergence of authority conflict with partitioning of exposure?
When does joint atomic closure conflict with failure-domain isolation?
Can one system centralize semantic truth while partitioning execution authority?
Does substrate availability (transactional vs external) change intervention type without changing the underlying invariant?
compression_rule: No generator name/rule is promoted until positive and negative worlds jointly identify moderators.
holdout_rule: Each surviving motif should receive a fresh out-of-stream challenge where practical; at minimum one fresh holdout must discriminate between competing motifs.
